title: E6 Set_Lane guard can never reject on auto pipes — the zero-check is dead code for the common path
detail: qos_auto_weights_after unconditionally sets in_play[c.lane]=true, and every in-play lane receives a positive ladder share (documented rows [100]/[70,30]/[50,30,20]). So for any auto pipe, w[c.lane]==0 is unreachable — the E6 rejection the comment promises ('the bus rejects the player's edit as the primary guard') cannot fire.
recommended_fix: Either keep a real guard (e.g. validate against current weights AND require the auto-follow to be written atomically with Set_Lane), or delete the dead branch and document that E6 bus rejection no longer applies to auto pipes.

title: Never-drop lane safety now depends on a non-core actor writing the auto-follow; validation outcome is command-order dependent
evidence:
+// sla_weights — append a logged Cmd_Set_Weights (the 5.8 auto-follow write —
+// the app records the ladder result after every categorization; scenarios that
+// categorize must mirror it, or the pipe sits on the 08-19 unconfigured
+// 100% Standard default).
detail: The guard validates against hypothetical post-auto-follow weights, but core never writes them — the app must. Any other command source (replay, harness, future callers) that omits the follow-up leaves a never-drop class permanently parked on a zero-weight lane with the bus's blessing. The test/demo patches prove the coupling: three demos and two fixtures had to be retrofitted to mirror the app.
recommended_fix: Make the auto-follow a core-side effect of applying Cmd_Set_Lane (or an atomic composite command), so the invariant the guard assumes is enforced where the state actually changes.

title: balance.json comment still documents the retired behavior as canon — the exact drift this change claims to eliminate
evidence: lane_presets = the 3.2 emphasis-dial positions (GDD M2 lever 2), per-pipe lane WFQ weights, data-driven — the 5.8 panel keeps them as manual quick-sets; default_lane_preset is the resting position every pipe starts on + the E5 all-zero fallback.
detail: The rewritten comment still says default_lane_preset is 'the resting position every pipe starts on + the E5 all-zero fallback', directly contradicting the same diff's catalog.odin comment ('The pipe RESTING default is NOT a preset') and the code (apply_draw/qos_pipe_caps now use qos_unconfigured_weights). The spec task was to rewrite this comment because documenting drift as canon caused the bug; a stale clause survives.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the default_lane_preset clause to state it is only the app-side manual quick-set default; name qos_unconfigured_weights as the resting and E5 fallback.

title: Spec marks itself done with all tasks checked, but omits the validate_set_lane semantic change, qos_auto_weights_after, and the palcheck change
location: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-v2-qos-default-standard.md (Code Map / Tasks) vs core/topology.odin + harness/palcheck.odin hunks
evidence:
- [x] `core/topology.odin` -- `apply_draw` appends `qos_unconfigured_weights(cat)`
 ... 
- `core/topology.odin` -- `apply_draw` appends the pipe's initial weights (line ~196)
detail: The spec's code map and task list cover only apply_draw for topology.odin, yet the diff changes validate_set_lane's E6 semantics and adds a new exported proc (qos_auto_weights_after); harness/palcheck.odin appears in no spec entry at all. The spec header reads status: 'done' with every box [x], so the contract misrepresents the shipped change set.
recommended_fix: Add the validate_set_lane rework, qos_auto_weights_after, and the palcheck oracle change to the spec's code map/tasks (and fill the empty Spec Change Log), or re-scope the diff.

title: qos_auto_weights_after copy-pastes qos_auto_weights' in-play/fold/distribute logic, and its fold reads pre-edit overrides
detail: The fold resolves never-drop lanes via qos_lane_of against pre-edit overrides, so when a never-drop class is MOVED, its old lane stays reserved and the guard validates against weights (e.g. 50/30/20) that are not the settled result (70/30). Benign today because the check is only ==0, but the two ladder copies can drift independently.
recommended_fix: Factor the shared in-play/fold/distribute body into one helper parameterized by an optional candidate override, so the guard and the settled computation cannot diverge.
